docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat search as two surfaces in code: an unfocused search bar state driven by Search - Bar tokens and an activated search view state driven by Search - View tokens.
  • Expressive contained search should animate outer margins from 24dp to 12dp on focus, keep the bar at 56dp tall, and preserve the 2dp gap between the docked bar and results surface.
  • Baseline divided search uses 16dp internal icon or text spacing, a 72dp full-screen header, a 56dp docked header, no rounding for full-screen results, and extra-large rounding for docked results.
  • Body text for both supporting and input content resolves to body-large metrics, so the same typography primitive can back the bar and the activated header text.
  • The live viewer exposes the search-bar motion spring only through its source token name, so any motion implementation should treat the spring family as specified but derive the exact damping value from the broader motion token source if that repository surface needs it later.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Sliders expose six active token sets in the live viewer: one common Slider set plus five expressive size sets from Slider - Size - Xsmall through Slider - Size - Xlarge.
  • The common set fixes the baseline active and inactive track height at 16dp, the standard handle at 44dp tall and 4dp wide, and the enabled active color on md.ref.palette.primary40 (#6750A4).
  • Expressive size sets scale track geometry from 16dp to 96dp and add inset-icon tokens from medium upward: medium and large use 24dp icons, while xlarge uses 32dp icons.
  • Disabled states mute the slider onto neutral tokens with 0.38 active-track and handle opacity and 0.12 inactive-track opacity.
  • The measurements chart and token viewer disagree on a few geometry values, notably the medium handle height and the label container height; the discrepancy is documented below instead of being flattened away.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat sliders as a common behavior surface plus expressive size overlays: the Slider token set owns state colors, stop indicators, value indicator styling, and default track or handle behavior, while the size sets only patch the geometry.
  • The enabled common slider uses primary40 for the active track and handle, secondary90 for the inactive track, and full rounding on track, handle, and stop indicators.
  • Disabled styling is driven by neutral tokens and explicit opacity rows rather than separate disabled palette tokens for every surface, so the implementation should preserve both the base color and the opacity.
  • Medium-and-up expressive sliders introduce inset icons through size-set tokens, but the measurements chart remains the source of truth for final preset dimensions when it conflicts with the token viewer.
  • Because the measurements chart and token viewer disagree on the medium handle height and the label container height, geometry presets in this repository should prefer the charted measurement values and use the token viewer primarily for colors, states, and ancillary spacing.

docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/snackbar/specs Collected: 2026-05-26

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Snackbar exposes one live component token set, Snackbars, and the visible spec context is Default, Light.
  • The enabled snackbar uses inverse roles: inverse-surface for the container, inverse-on-surface for supporting text and the optional icon, and inverse-primary for the action label.
  • Geometry is compact and fixed: the single-line container is 48dp tall, the two-line container token is 68dp, the container shape is extra-small rounding, and the container elevation resolves to 6dp.
  • The measurement figure shows 16dp leading content padding, 8dp trailing padding after the action, and a close affordance built from a 24dp icon with 12dp padding on both sides.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat snackbars as inverse surfaces rather than standard surface containers: container fill uses inverse-surface, action emphasis uses inverse-primary, and supporting or close-affordance content uses inverse-on-surface.
  • The component exposes two explicit height variants, 48dp for single-line and 68dp for two-line content, so layout code should switch variants instead of stretching a single base geometry.
  • Action typography maps cleanly to label-large, while supporting text maps to body-medium; that is enough to derive the preview-only *.type rows without custom typography tokens.
  • The optional close affordance fits a 48dp wide touch target when the figure's 12dp + 24dp + 12dp spacing is applied.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Drive split-button geometry from the size token set first (xsmall through xlarge), with a constant between-space of 2dp.
  • Keep leading/trailing horizontal spacing size-specific; those values increase significantly at Large and Xlarge and should not be derived from a simple linear scale.
  • Preserve state-specific inner corner transitions (hovered and pressed) and trailing-button selected inner corner (50%) for correct split-joint appearance.
  • Treat container.shape as preview-driven in this source; use concrete corner-size tokens where provided (inner-corner and Xsmall outer-corner) for implementation math.
  • Keep split-button color behavior aligned with standard button specs; selected state applies a state layer without changing the base color role.

docs.title: Switch MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/switch/specs Collected: 2026-05-26

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Switch exposes one active token set in the live viewer: Switch with Default, Light context chips.
  • The component uses a 52dp by 32dp track with a 2dp outline, a 40dp state layer, and a 48dp minimum touch target.
  • Handle sizes step between 16dp unselected, 24dp selected or with-icon, and 28dp pressed; enabled handle elevation is md.sys.elevation.level1 and disabled handle elevation drops to md.sys.elevation.level0.
  • Selected states pair md.sys.color.primary track or icon treatments with an md.sys.color.on-primary enabled handle and md.sys.color.primary-container hovered, focused, and pressed handle treatments.
  • Unselected states keep the track and icon on md.sys.color.surface-container-highest, use md.sys.color.outline for track outlines, and switch to md.sys.color.on-surface for state-layer overlays.
  • Focus adds a dedicated indicator on md.sys.color.secondary with a 3dp thickness and a 2dp offset.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Model the switch as a 52dp by 32dp track inside a 48dp target, with a 40dp circular state layer centered on the control.
  • Size the handle by configuration and state rather than one fixed thumb size: 16dp unselected, 24dp selected or with-icon, and 28dp pressed.
  • Keep selected track and selected icon treatments on md.sys.color.primary, pair the enabled selected handle with md.sys.color.on-primary, and move the selected hover, focus, and pressed handle fills to md.sys.color.primary-container.
  • Keep unselected track and icon fills on md.sys.color.surface-container-highest, use md.sys.color.outline for unselected outlines, and use md.sys.color.on-surface for unselected hover, focus, and pressed state-layer overlays.
  • Support the dedicated focus ring: md.comp.switch.focus.indicator.* maps to the MD3 focus-indicator system tokens with a 3dp thickness and 2dp outer offset.
  • The viewer still exposes legacy handle shadow, size, and elevation tokens. Treat those rows as deprecated and prefer the selected, unselected, pressed, and with-icon token families for new implementation work.

docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/tabs/specs Collected: 2026-05-26

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Tabs exposes two active token sets in the live viewer: Tabs - Primary navigation and Tabs - Secondary navigation, both under the Default, Light context.
  • Both variants use equal-width tab sections, square containers on md.sys.shape.corner.none, 48dp label-only height, 64dp icon-plus-label height, a 1dp divider, and 24dp icons.
  • Primary tabs drive the active indicator, active label, and active icon from md.sys.color.primary, while inactive label and icon treatments stay on md.sys.color.on-surface-variant.
  • Secondary tabs keep the active indicator on md.sys.color.primary, but active label and icon treatments stay on md.sys.color.on-surface; inactive label and icon treatments remain on md.sys.color.on-surface-variant.
  • Both variants share md.sys.typescale.title-small for tab labels, use hover opacity 0.08, focus and pressed opacity 0.1, and expose a secondary-colored focus indicator with 3dp thickness and a -3dp inner offset.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Implement both tab variants as square-corner containers with equal-width slots, a 1dp internal divider, and 48dp or 64dp heights depending on whether the tab shows only text or both icon and label.
  • Reuse md.sys.typescale.title-small for tab labels in both variants; the extracted component rows resolve to 14pt size, 20pt line height, 500 weight, and 0.1pt tracking.
  • Keep the primary-tab active indicator, active icon, and active label on md.sys.color.primary, but keep inactive icon and label treatments on md.sys.color.on-surface-variant and inactive hover or focus overlays on md.sys.color.on-surface.
  • Keep the secondary-tab active indicator on md.sys.color.primary while leaving the active icon and active label on md.sys.color.on-surface; inactive label and icon treatments still use md.sys.color.on-surface-variant.
  • Model the focus affordance with md.comp.*.focus.indicator.*: both variants resolve to md.sys.color.secondary, 3dp thickness, and a -3dp inner offset, while hover uses 0.08 opacity and focus or pressed uses 0.1 opacity.

docs.title: Text Fields MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/text-fields/specs Collected: 2026-04-27

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Material Design 3 text field specifications covering filled and outlined fields plus current select and autocomplete variants exposed in the live token viewer.
  • Five interactive states are represented across the current token sets: Enabled, Disabled, Hovered, Focused, and Error.
  • Values were resolved from the Material token table using the Light + Default + Expressive context when available, with Light + Default as fallback.

docs.title: Interactive (tappable) icons — design note
docs.text:
Investigated for #302 (2026-07-11).

The text-field token set models the leading / trailing icon as decorative only: the icon tokens are colors per field state ({hover,focus,error,disabled}.{leading,trailing}-icon.color) and a 24dp size, describing how the glyph is tinted while the field is in that state. Both hover.trailing-icon.color and the enabled trailing-icon.color resolve to #49454F, confirming the token describes field state, not a hover of the icon itself. There is no icon state-layer token in any text-field set — the only state-layer tokens are for the filled field's own container.

MD3 does not spell out a token for an interactive text-field icon. The governing principle is stated generally: "Apply states consistently across components," and the Enabled state description ("An enabled state communicates an interactive component… Enabled states use the default styling for each interactive component") means an interactive element is expected to carry the usual state layers. Following the Flutter and Jetpack Compose implementations, an interactive text-field icon is therefore realized as a standard icon button (md.comp.icon-button.standard.*), which brings hover (8%), focus (10%), and pressed state layers plus keyboard focusability.

Implementation: in TextField, a leading / trailing icon with a tap callback (on_tap_leading_icon / on_tap_trailing_icon) is built as a standard IconButton; a decorative icon (no callback) stays a plain, feedback-free Icon. Hit testing is handled by the framework's coordinate-translating widget tree (offset-safe; see #300), not a field-local rectangle test.

Known gap: the framework has no mouse-cursor-shape API, so the pointer does not change to a hand over the tappable icon (no existing widget changes the cursor either). Tracked separately in #316.

docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/time-pickers/specs Collected: 2026-03-12

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The primary token viewer exposes two non-deprecated token sets: Time picker - Dial and Time picker - Input.
  • Dial tokens define a 256dp clock dial with a 48dp selector handle, 8dp selector center, 2dp selector track, and 96dp x 80dp time-selector cells; the horizontal period selector expands to 216dp x 38dp.
  • Input tokens define dynamic outer container sizing with 96dp x 72dp time-input fields and a 52dp x 72dp period selector.
  • Both variants resolve their outer container elevation through md.sys.elevation.level3; the outer containers use 28dp extra-large rounding while selector and input subcontainers resolve to 8dp small-corner shapes.
  • Hover state-layer opacity is 0.08; focus and pressed state-layer opacity are 0.1 across the exposed interactive tokens.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat dial and input variants as separate widget implementations. The dial variant adds dedicated clock-dial geometry, selector center, selector track, and selector-handle tokens, while the input variant adds focused-container and focus-indicator tokens.
  • Shape and elevation rows are not fully exposed inline in the viewer. The detail popups resolve them through system tokens such as md.sys.shape.corner.extra-large, md.sys.shape.corner.small, md.sys.shape.corner.full, and md.sys.elevation.level3.
  • Typography .type rows are composite preview tokens. The viewer also exposes scalar font, size, line-height, weight, and tracking rows, which are the more direct implementation inputs.
  • The dial token set includes *.ignore clock-dial tokens marked with a warning badge. Keep them out of default implementation paths unless you intentionally need to mirror the source exactly.
  • The accessible Measurements tables for vertical and horizontal dial layouts currently expose the same numeric rows in the live DOM, so the page does not provide different orientation-specific numeric callouts beyond the shared table values.

docs.title: Toolbars MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/toolbars/specs Collected: 2026-05-26

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The active toolbar viewer exposes five current token sets under the Default, Light context: Toolbar - Color - Standard, Toolbar - Color - Vibrant, Toolbar - Docked, Toolbar - Floating, and Toolbar - Floating - FAB.
  • The deprecated Bottom app bar (baseline) remains on the page in a separate viewer, but the spec explicitly marks it as not recommended and this document skips its token rows.
  • Docked toolbars are square 64dp containers with 16dp leading and trailing padding and 4dp to 32dp action spacing, while floating toolbars keep the same 64dp height with a full shape, 8dp internal side padding, 16dp horizontal edge margin, 24dp vertical edge margin, and 6dp elevation.
  • Standard color toolbars use md.sys.color.surface-container for the toolbar and unselected button container with selected buttons on md.sys.color.secondary-container; vibrant toolbars switch the base container to md.sys.color.primary-container and selected buttons back to md.sys.color.surface-container.
  • Floating toolbars with FAB add an 8dp gap between the toolbar and FAB, support 56dp and 80dp FAB sizes, use 24dp or 28dp FAB icons, and resolve their FAB corners and elevations from the MD3 large and large-increased shape tokens plus elevation levels 1 and 2.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat toolbar geometry and toolbar color as separate concerns: Toolbar - Docked, Toolbar - Floating, and Toolbar - Floating - FAB define layout and shape, while the standard and vibrant color sets define the actual container and action colors.
  • Prefer docked and floating toolbars for new work. The spec page keeps the baseline bottom app bar only as a legacy fallback and explicitly recommends the docked toolbar instead.
  • Floating toolbars share the same standard-vs-vibrant color split as docked toolbars, but floating adds a 6dp elevated container and distinct horizontal vs vertical edge margins.
  • The floating FAB variant needs two FAB sizes in addition to the toolbar itself: 56dp with a 24dp icon and 16dp corner radius for the expanded FAB, and 80dp with a 28dp icon and 20dp corner radius for the medium FAB.
  • The extracted values here reflect the live Default, Light viewer context. Dark, contrast, and platform-specific variants remain available through the underlying contextual token tree but are intentionally out of scope for this document.

docs.title: Tooltips MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/tooltips/specs Collected: 2026-05-26

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The tooltip spec page exposes two current token sets under the live Default, Light context: Tooltip - Plain and Tooltip - Rich.
  • Plain tooltips are compact inverse-surface containers: 24dp high, 8dp padded, 4dp corner radius, with inverse-on-surface supporting text set in body-small typography.
  • Rich tooltips are elevated surface containers: 12dp corner radius, 3dp elevation, surface-container fill, on-surface-variant text, and primary-colored action text and state layers.
  • The current typography ramp resolves to Google Sans Text for plain supporting text, rich subheads, rich supporting text, and rich action labels.
  • Rich tooltip configurations allow an optional headline and up to two text buttons; the measurements figure only specifies padding, so overall height remains content-driven.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Plain tooltips can be modeled as fixed-height inverse surfaces with a single supporting-text slot. The extracted token set only exposes enabled-state styling, so hover or pressed container variants are not part of this component.
  • Rich tooltips split structure and action styling cleanly: the container owns surface, shape, elevation, subhead, and supporting-text tokens, while actions reuse primary-colored label and state-layer tokens with hover 0.08, focus 0.1, and pressed 0.1 opacities.
  • The current live spec resolves typography to Google Sans Text, not the older Roboto-based ramp that appears in some previously collected MD3 docs in this repository.
  • Rich tooltip height should be treated as content-driven. The spec only gives padding, elevation, and corner geometry, then documents five content configurations ranging from body-only to subhead plus supporting text plus two buttons.
